$comment: SHA-256 + code-point count + section-tag count of the RAW Cowork system-prompt constant (the module-scope backtick-template string consumed once as system_prompts.cowork_system_prompt.value.prompt) extracted from each Claude Desktop app.asar. Purpose: let a maintainer detect prompt-append DRIFT across Desktop releases WITHOUT publishing the proprietary verbatim text — the committed baselines/prompts/desktop-*/system-prompt-append.md are deliberately PARAPHRASED under the repo's no-bundling rule. This is prompt-SPECIFIC and complements provenance.asarFingerprint in baselines/desktop-*.json, which is a coarse 16-char hash over broad cowork slices and flips on any nearby churn (e.g. a minifier rename), not only on prompt content.
extractionMethod: In the Desktop app.asar bundle, find the single consumption site `cowork_system_prompt:{value:{prompt:<id>}` and read the minified constant <id> (name is minifier-assigned and varies per build). Take the backtick-template body of `<id>=`...``. TWO hashes are recorded. sha256 + codePoints are over the RAW template SOURCE (${} placeholders and \-escapes left intact) -- minifier-NAME-independent, and the committed history. decodedSha256 + decodedCodePoints are over the same body with \n \t \r \xXX \uXXXX \u{...} escapes DECODED, i.e. the string the engine actually produces. COMPARE ON THE DECODED PAIR: Desktop 1.32352.0 changed codegen to escape non-ASCII, which moved the raw sha by +630 code points while the rendered prompt stayed byte-identical -- a raw-only comparison cannot tell that from real drift. A raw-only move is a re-stamp, not a paraphrase re-derivation. codePoints = [...body].length; sectionTags = count of /<([a-z_]+)>/g opens.
localRawRetention: The verbatim raw is retained locally (NEVER committed) under ~/cowork-agent-backup/desktop-asar/<ver>/cowork-system-prompt-raw.txt, alongside a full app.asar backup — see the Desktop-asar backup ritual in the private CLAUDE.md.

1.18286.0.note: Recorded before this fingerprint file existed; the 1.18286.0 asar was pruned by the Desktop self-update before a hash could be captured, and old Desktop versions are not re-downloadable. codePoints + sectionTags are from the reconstruction (docs/internal). Presumed byte-identical to 1.18286.2 on the strength of an exact code-point + section-tag-structure match.

1.18286.2.note: First release with a retained raw + hash anchor. Prompt append verified UNCHANGED vs 1.18286.0 (identical 37857 code points and identical 43-tag section structure/order); the reconstructed 1.18286.0 paraphrase baseline remains faithful for 1.18286.2.

1.19367.0.note: Back-filled 2026-07-10 from the retained asar backup. Prompt append BYTE-IDENTICAL to 1.18286.2 (same SHA-256, same 37857 code points / 43 tags); only the minifier-assigned constant id changed (sIi -> JDr). The 1.18286.0 paraphrase baseline remains faithful.

1.20186.0.note: Prompt CHANGED vs 1.19367.0: +18 code points, purely additive (37933-byte prefix identical; trailing bytes = '\n{{modelIdentity}}' appended after </env>), section-tag structure unchanged (43 opens / 40 unique names). The {{modelIdentity}} placeholder is DEPLOYMENT-GATED: rendered only for custom-3p/enterprise deployments; on the first-party Cowork the harness emulates (deployment class type='1p', rendererConfig()=null) the renderer takes the strip branch (/\n?\{\{modelIdentity\}\}/g -> '') so the RENDERED prompt is byte-identical to pre-1.20186.0. The 1.18286.0 paraphrase baseline therefore remains faithful (no new paraphrase dir / renderer change). placeholders + sectionTagNames are consumed by the sync-time prompt-inventory drift-diff.

1.21459.0.note: Back-filled 2026-07-15 from the live asar during the 1.21459.0 parity sync. Prompt append BYTE-IDENTICAL to 1.20186.0 (same SHA-256, 37875 code points, 43 tags); only the minifier-assigned constant id changed (tOt -> f3t). 1.21459.0 wires a new claudeDesign SP section + a CLAUDE_DESIGN_TOOLS spawn-tool spread, both DEPLOYMENT-GATED OFF on first-party (design tools resolve to [] -> hasClaudeDesign=false -> the section is stripped and the tool is not spawned), so the RENDERED first-party prompt is unchanged and the 1.18286.0 paraphrase baseline remains faithful.

1.30096.1.note: Captured 2026-08-14 during the 1.30096.1 sync. Prompt append BYTE-IDENTICAL to 1.21459.0 and 1.20186.0 (same SHA-256, 37875 code points, 43 tags, same 10 placeholders and 40 section names); only the minifier-assigned constant id changed (f3t -> Xut) and the constant relocated chunks. Re-extracted independently via the documented extractionMethod, not inferred from an absent diff row. NOTE: entries for 1.22209.3 through 1.28929.0 were never back-filled; the prompt sha has not moved since 1.20186.0 so the drift check stayed green across that gap, but the gap is real and this entry does not close it.

1.32352.0.note: Captured 2026-08-18. The RAW sha moved (+630 code points) ONLY because the 1.32352.0 codegen began emitting non-ASCII as \uXXXX escapes (em dash, rightwards arrow). The RENDERED prompt is BYTE-IDENTICAL: both builds decode to 37811 code points / a14592804dfc..., and a diff of the two decoded bodies is empty. The prompt has therefore not changed since 1.20186.0 and the 1.18286.0 paraphrase baseline remains faithful. This entry is what motivated decodedSha256: hashing the RAW template source is minifier-NAME-independent but NOT escape-form-independent, so a raw-only comparison cannot tell a codegen change from real drift.

1.32885.1.note: Cowork system prompt BYTE-IDENTICAL to 1.32352.0 on both the raw and the decoded hash (38505 raw / 37811 decoded code points, 43 tags, same 10 placeholders); only the minifier-assigned constant id rotated umt -> Zlt. Raw retained locally per localRawRetention.

Corroborated by a SECOND source rather than by re-running the same extractor: the retained raw files for 1.32885.1, 1.34493.1, 1.37937.0 and 1.37937.1 are byte-identical to each other on disk (cmp), so the prompt has not moved since 1.20186.0.

1.37937.1.note: Desktop self-updated 1.37937.0 -> 1.37937.1 mid-pass. Prompt BYTE-IDENTICAL to 1.37937.0, same constant id Qgt. Recorded separately because provenance.asarFingerprint is the SAME 16-char value on both builds (it hashes only the cowork slices), so the baseline's own fingerprint cannot distinguish them and this file is where that distinction is kept.

subagentAppendMethod: Independent of the single-text `versions` fingerprints above: the sub-agent environment append is a TWO-BRANCH generator selected on hostLoopMode. In the SINGLE bundle module that references buildSubagentEnvironmentPrompt AND contains both branch discriminators, slice each branch's raw backtick-template body by scanning outward from its discriminator fragment (escaped backticks are decoded to bare backticks; other escapes left intact); DECODE escapes (same decoder as decodedSha256 -- 1.32352.0's codegen escape change moved BOTH branch fingerprints while the rendered branch text was byte-identical), then normalize every ${...} interpolation to the literal token ${} ; sha256 the UTF-8 bytes; keep the first 16 hex chars. The hl (host-loop) branch is discriminated by the fragment 'on the user's machine' (anchored to the occurrence immediately preceding the vm branch, since the phrase also occurs in unrelated prose), the vm (sandbox) branch by 'exist only in the sandbox'. BOTH fingerprints are mandatory per version entry. Consumed by checkSubagentPromptFacts in src/sync/cowork-sync.ts; re-derive with readMainBundleFiles + extractSubagentBranchSlices + subagentBranchFingerprint (see docs/maintenance.md). Raw texts retained locally only (see localRawRetention).

1.20186.1.note: Branch template texts byte-identical across 1.20186.0 and 1.20186.1 (both derive hl=8fe5583c5996776a, vm=859aa136fc15b38f). The named buildSubagentEnvironmentPrompt generator with these branch bodies is present from 1.20186.0; earlier retained releases (<=1.19367.0) used a differently-structured generator not covered by this fingerprint. Only the newest entry is compared, so one entry covers the current verified family.

1.32885.1.note: hl branch text CHANGED at this release (8fe5583c5996776a -> 71e028bfa7ce596d): one sentence appended stating that each shell command starts at the VM session root and that writes outside <root>/mnt/ (including /tmp) never reach the user or the sub-agent's file tools. Additive only - the preceding text is byte-identical, and the substitution-value proofs still hold (working directory ${hostCwd??vmRoot}, mounts ${vmRoot}/mnt/). NOT a codegen-escape artifact: the fingerprint decodes escapes before hashing (D8) and the vm branch is unchanged at 859aa136fc15b38f, which an escape-form change would also have moved. Paraphrase re-derived into baselines/prompts/desktop-1.32885.1/subagent-append-hl.md; the 1.20186.1 entry covers 1.20186.0 through 1.32352.0.

1.46388.3.note: Desktop 1.46388.3 REPLACED the hl branch and RESTRUCTURED the append into three parts. (1) hl 71e028bfa7ce596d -> 464ecc87a6810941: the whole paragraph was swapped for one sentence about the shell tool's cwd and non-visible writes. The host-filesystem framing, the working-directory value and the read/write-only-inside-attached-folders instruction did NOT vanish - they moved OUT of the server-overridable section into the new folder manifest, so the hl asset is no longer the whole hl append. (2) NEW `manifest` axis: an hl-ONLY block appended after resolveSection/the substituter, listing the outputs dir and each attached folder with its host<->shell mapping, with a separate prose variant when the list is empty. (3) NEW `suffix` axis: one sentence about invoking skills, appended UNCONDITIONALLY to BOTH branches - which is why vm stays 859aa136fc15b38f while the rendered vm append changed. That is the fail-open these two axes close: through 1.44121.1 the sentinel fingerprinted only the ternary arms, so a release adding only the suffix would have synced green on both branches (reproduced by counterfactual). Only the NEWEST entry is compared and only on the axes IT declares, so the 1.20186.1 and 1.32885.1 entries are not retro-failed for lacking manifest/suffix; once either is recorded both are mandatory. All four values are computed over normalizeBundleQuotes-NORMALIZED text (as the branch fingerprints always have been): that fold turns the manifest's interpolation-free join separator into a quoted string, so `manifest` covers exactly the six prose templates and no code. Paraphrases: hl re-derived into baselines/prompts/desktop-1.46388.3/subagent-append-hl.md; the manifest is GENERATED (src/prompt/subagent-manifest.ts) because it is built from live mount state and no static file can be faithful - same reasoning as the main-loop section in src/runtime/hostloop-prompt.ts; the suffix is carried in BOTH the hl and vm assets.
